column3: ## Successfully upload a file containing rich text (JATS) formatting in the title and abstract

Setup: Ensure that the publisher account owns a journal with Print ISSN "1111-1111" and E-ISSN "2222-2222", and these are not attached to any other journals, and that this journal does not already contain a "Rich text" article from a previous run of this test (delete it via the admin interface if it does).
Setup: You must be logged in using a pure publisher account (no other privileges)
Setup: You will also need an administrator account for the final step

Go to the "Upload Article XML" tab in the "Publisher Area"

http://testdoaj.cottagelabs.com//publisher/uploadfile

Browse for a file under "Select a file" and select the test resource file "jats_rich_text.xml" from the Crossref 5.3.1 resources

Test Resource: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DOAJ/doaj/feature/2861_abstract_rich_text/doajtest/xml_upload_test_package/Crossref/5.3.1/jats_rich_text.xml
Choose "Crossref 5.3.1 XML" from "Format of the file" dropdown

column4: A flash message appears at the top of the screen indicating a successful upload
Your file is shown in the "History of uploads" with status "pending"

column3: wait a short amount of time for the job to process, then reload the page (do not re-submit the form data). If the job remains in "pending", reload the page until the status changes.

column4: Your file is shown in the "History of uploads" with status "successfully processed", and the Note "1 articles imported (1 new, 0 updated)"

column3:
Go to the Table of Contents for the journal (e.g. by going to /toc/2222-2222), and go to the Articles tab

http://testdoaj.cottagelabs.com//toc/2222-2222

column4: The list of articles contains an article titled "Rich text TiOx/Pt3Ti(111) and E=mc2", where the "x" is an italic subscript, the "3" is a subscript and the "2" is a superscript
No literal tags such as "<sub>", "<i>" or "<sub>" are visible in the title

column3: Click "Abstract" on that article to expand it

column4: The abstract reads "Films grown on a Pt3Ti(111) surface. Phases z-TiOx and w-TiOx were produced. Energy scales as c2. Second paragraph with <script>alert('xss')</script> text."
The "3" in "Pt3Ti" is a subscript, each "x" in "TiOx" is an italic subscript, the word "produced" is bold, and the "2" in "c2" is a superscript
No text from the abstract is missing (in particular "Ti(111) surface", which follows the first subscript, is present)
The text "<script>alert('xss')</script>" is shown literally as plain text; no alert pop-up appears

column3: Click the article title to open the public article page

column4: The page heading shows the title with the same subscript/superscript/italic formatting as on the Table of Contents, with no literal tags visible
The abstract shows the same formatting as on the Table of Contents, and the "<script>alert('xss')</script>" text is shown literally with no alert pop-up
The browser tab title shows the article title as plain text ("Rich text TiOx/Pt3Ti(111) and E=mc2 ...") with no "<sub>", "<i>" or "<sup>" tags in it

column3: View the page source of the article page and find the "citation_title" meta tag

column4: The content of the "citation_title" meta tag is "Rich text TiOx/Pt3Ti(111) and E=mc2" with no HTML tags in it

column3:
Go to the public article search and search for "Rich text TiOx"

http://testdoaj.cottagelabs.com//search/articles

column4: The article is found and its title and (expanded) abstract are rendered with the same formatting as on the Table of Contents, with no literal tags visible

column3:
Log in as an administrator, go to the "Journals & Articles" search in the admin area and search for "Rich text TiOx"

http://testdoaj.cottagelabs.com//admin/admin_site_search

column4: The article's title is shown with the same formatting, with no literal tags visible
Click "(show/hide)" next to the Abstract; the abstract is shown with the same formatting, and "<script>alert('xss')</script>" is shown literally with no alert pop-up
